name: Flash on the turn of the film
visual_intent: Mark the one or two biggest turns of a film with a flash under which the scene changes; pair it with the hit.

parameters.name: color
parameters.description: White reads as exposure on a dark frame; on the light canvas use an accent or the radial shape

parameters.name: shape
parameters.description: flat (whole frame) or radial (burst centred on the incoming subject)

parameters.name: decay
parameters.description: Seconds from full flash to clear (0.15-0.35 in the references)

parameters.name: preDim
parameters.description: Seconds the outgoing scene darkens before the flash

timeline_requirements.gsap_instance: Timeline passed to Studio.build(builder) (registered as window.__timelines['root'])
timeline_requirements.timing_anchors: Cue map (Studio.cues) or word times (Studio.cues.fromWords); place it on the word or beat it illustrates

code_snippet.javascript:
// the hit lands 0-250 ms after the flash; at most two or three per film
Studio.fx.flash(tl, '#s2', '#s3', cue('turn'), { shape: 'radial', color: Studio.token('--c-accent-3'), center: '#s3 h1', preDim: 0.2 });

fallbacks: Studio.cut on the beat with the hit alone, or Studio.fx.bloom when an element can carry the change.

performance_characteristics.memory_impact: Low; estimate, not measured on the M2

validation_steps: python scripts/frame-review.py tests/reference-derived/flash-and-container/index.html --serve-root . --fonts google --at <cue, cue + 1 frame, cue + decay>
On the render host: hyperframes snapshot at the cue and one frame after; count flashes per second for WCAG 2.3.1

validation.evidence: Runtime checks tests/studio-runtime/backlog-techniques.html in Playwright Chromium on Windows, 2026-11-28.
